findings.what: The entry offers 'the same two checks' for -58's two wrap parts, but leaves out that the two figures read only measured ticks (the frozen SERIES rows: 'measured tick records only'; CB-P8's test). -58 reads the whole run because its wraps fall in the first seconds (marks.json PM-0001-58 notes: 'The whole run is read (window: all): the wraps fall in the first seconds'). As written, then, the checks would not see the wrap ticks. A real bound needs wrap runs that put the wraps inside the measured window, or a whole-run reading of the figures, and the second changes what a figure computes, which needs his yes. Option (a) is therefore bigger than the entry says. Both options already go through his yes on the exact wording, so nothing wrong can be built.

U4g already takes -58 and will likely change marks.json (advisor-c62h-review-full.md:90), so one wording yes and one reviewer's read under his 13:35 rule cover both -58 and -17's B1 part. That design work belongs where the wrap runs are designed, so a separate lane now (a) would do it twice or do it blind. Option (c) is acceptable but leaves a known hiding place open with no owner. The lab now records which snapshot packets the simulated network lost. The judge has two new checks on PM-0001-17:
- every tick a client files as lost must be explained: either the room sent nothing that tick, or the network lost a packet of it;
- no tick may arrive whole while the network says it lost a packet of it.

Results:
- On all six clean ten-minute runs (P2 and P3, three seeds each), both checks read 0. The lab's own count of unexplained ticks agrees with the judge's every time.
- Each planted bug reads exactly 48 on its own check, with every other check passing.

So simply copying the checks would miss the wraps. Either the wrap runs are set up so the wraps fall inside the measured window, or the checks gain a whole-run reading. The second changes what a check computes, so it would come to you as exact wording for a yes.
